questions.question: Before a trip, you can make sure air flows to all trailers by:

options.text: Checking for moving air inside each trailer.
Listening for air at the rear shut-off valve.
Feeling for air at the front shut-off valve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listening for air at the rear shut-off valve.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check that air reaches all trailers. Open the shut-off valves on the rear of the last trailer. If air escapes from these valves, air is reaching the entire vehicle.

questions.question: In a vehicle with an automatic tractor protection valve, the valve will pop out when air pressure drops to:

options.text: 20 and 45 psi.
75 and 105 psi.
50 and 65 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: 20 and 45 psi.
questions.explanation: The automatic tractor protection valve will pop out if air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, the valve closes and stops air flow.

questions.question: When backing up your tractor to couple it to a trailer, the trailer brakes should be:

options.text: Deactivated.
Locked.
Unlocked.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locked.
questions.explanation: Before backing your tractor under the trailer, lock the trailer brakes. This is important for safe coupling.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to jackknife, the driver:

options.text: Should not apply the trailer hand brake.
Should firmly apply the brakes.
Can straighten the trailer with the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not apply the trailer hand brake.
questions.explanation: If a trailer jackknifes, release the brakes to let the wheels regain traction. Do not apply the trailer hand brake because brakes caused the wheels to lock in the first place.

questions.question: When coupling a trailer:

options.text: Make sure to couple the proper glad hands.
Glad hands can be connected to any other glad hands.
Only one set of glad hands should be connected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure to couple the proper glad hands.
questions.explanation: Couple matching glad hands. They are often color-coded: blue for service lines and red for emergency lines.

questions.question: What is the tractor protection valve?

options.text: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if a bad leak occurs.
A valve that prevents the trailer from being accidentally released.
A valve that prevents the vehicle from going too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if a bad leak occurs.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a bad leak. It closes automatically when pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: To prevent a rollover, cargo should be:

options.text: Loaded with most weight on the driver's side of the trailer.
Placed near the rear of the trailer.
Spread out evenly in the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spread out evenly in the trailer.
questions.explanation: Distribute cargo weight evenly throughout the trailer to reduce rollover risk. Do not put too much weight on one side.

questions.question: When braking while pulling a trailer with anti-lock brakes, you should:

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Use extra braking force to ensure the brakes work.
Brake the same way as you would without anti-lock brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way as you would without anti-lock brakes.
questions.explanation: Brake the same way whether or not the vehicle has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: When coupling:

options.text: You can assume all vehicles are the same.
Make sure you are coupling correctly.
Cracks in the mounting are acceptable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure you are coupling correctly.
questions.explanation: Incorrect coupling and uncoupling can cause serious accidents.

questions.question: A combination vehicle has ____ air line(s).

options.text: One
Two
Three

questions.correctAnswerText: Two
questions.explanation: Every combination vehicle has two air lines: the service line and the emergency line.

questions.question: Combination vehicles:

options.text: Are usually shorter than single commercial vehicles.
Usually require less skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
Usually require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles require more skill to drive. They are longer, heavier, and more likely to roll over than single commercial vehicles.

questions.question: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Sit in the cab and call for help.
Exit the cab and walk away from the tracks.
Motion for another driver to push your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the cab and walk away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, exit immediately and walk away from the tracks. Then call emergency authorities.

questions.question: To control surge when stopping, you should not:

options.text: Keep a steady pressure on the brakes.
Brake well in advance of a stop.
Release the brakes too quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brakes too quickly.
questions.explanation: To prevent surge in a tank vehicle, keep steady brake pressure and do not release the brakes too early. Brake ahead of time and increase your distance from other vehicles.

questions.question: Bobtail tractors are ____ to stop than tractors attached to full semitrailers.

options.text: Quicker
Easier
More difficult

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor with no semitrailer attached. Bobtails are hard to stop and take longer to come to a complete stop than tractors pulling loaded semitrailers.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, you must turn the steering wheel:

options.text: In the direction you want the trailer to move.
In the direction opposite of where you want the trailer to move.
To the left until backing is complete.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction opposite of where you want the trailer to move.
questions.explanation: When backing a trailer, turn the steering wheel the opposite way from where you want the trailer to go. Once the trailer starts turning, turn the steering wheel the other way to follow it.

questions.question: If the emergency air line loses pressure:

options.text: The service brakes will activate.
The tractor protection valve will close.
The rear trailer will detach from the combination.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tractor protection valve will close.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the trailer's brakes if the trailer breaks away or leaks. When air pressure in the emergency line drops, the tractor protection valve closes and the trailer emergency brakes activate.

questions.question: If a parked trailer does not have spring brakes, you should keep the trailer from moving by:

options.text: Having the vehicle parked against a wall or other vehicle.
Using chock blocks.
Parking on a slight incline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using chock blocks.
questions.explanation: If a parked trailer has no spring brakes, use wheel chocks to prevent it from rolling.

questions.question: In a double or triple combination, the ____ trailer should be directly behind the cab.

options.text: Lightest
Heaviest
Smallest

questions.correctAnswerText: Heaviest
questions.explanation: In a combination of multiple trailers, the heaviest loaded trailer should be closest to the tractor. The lightest trailer should be at the rear.

questions.question: Shut-off valves:

options.text: Prevent air from escaping air brake systems.
Prevent air from entering air brake systems.
Override vehicles that are out of control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent air from escaping air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers. The rear shut-off valve should always be closed to keep air from leaving the braking system.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor without a semi-trailer
A tractor with two semi-trailers
A tractor that travels faster than the speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: A tractor without a semi-trailer
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor with no semitrailer. Drivers must be careful operating bobtails because they are difficult to handle.
